data.one_liner: An HTTP inspection and debugging tool for Flutter apps.
data.what_it_does: Chuck catches and stores HTTP requests and responses, providing a simple built-in UI to view headers, payloads, errors, and statistics. It supports Dio, dart:io HttpClient, and any other HTTP client via a client-agnostic logging API.
use_when: You need to inspect and debug HTTP traffic directly inside your Flutter app.
You want a floating inspector button or shake gesture to view network calls during development.
avoid_when: You are in a strict production-only environment where network payload storage overhead must be completely avoided (unless disabled).
You need an external desktop proxy tool like Charles Proxy or Fiddler instead of an in-app viewer.
strengths: Supports Dio, HttpClient, and custom/client-agnostic HTTP logging.
Comes with a floating call counter button and shake-to-open capabilities.
Provides curl command generation and call search/filtering.
weaknesses: Requires passing a navigator key or using app builder to display the UI.
Stores HTTP request and response history in memory, which needs sizing limits for heavy traffic.
data.setup_notes: Initialize Chuck, pass the navigator key to MaterialApp, and add the Dio interceptor or use the client-agnostic API.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: Dio is an HTTP client with its own robust interceptor ecosystem if you only need network handling and basic logging without a standalone UI overlay.
